items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Reach across water - Campaign and Settle across a sea leg, staged from harbour works, so colonisation by a major is the Metropole played overseas
items.design:
THE GAP. The sim knows enclosed-sea ring closure (w_ring) and nothing else about water: no Campaign or Settle target lies across a sea leg, so "the extent of colonisation by major powers" cannot be produced by pass 2 at all. The works roster already authors the rows that should gate it - Harbour Mole, Deepwater Wharf, Naval Yard, Coaling Station - and they do nothing for reach today.

THE DESIGN, in the sim's own currency. A sea leg is a candidate-grain extension of the target set: a region reachable by a coastal walk from a staging hub that holds a harbour work, with the leg's supply cost read from the same reach substrate the land term uses (one reach field, BL-325 ruling 3) and its range capped by the hub's best harbour row (Mole: littoral; Wharf: the enclosed sea; Naval Yard: open water; Coaling Station: any coast). Settle across the leg founds a holding that counts toward holdings_burden_q like any other - the burden of breadth is what makes an overseas empire strain, and reach-fed strain (COLLAPSE.md § 5, the Metropole's inevitability) is the accumulator it feeds. A colony is therefore expensive to hold and worth holding, and the major that holds too many culminates. Non-hegemony (BL-224, the non-hegemony invariant) is not relaxed for the sea: 1960 arrives multipolar.

BOUNDED BY CONSTRUCTION like the land verbs: two staging hubs per polity per round (the capital and one rotated coastal holding), candidate legs from those only. Deterministic - the coastal walk is over sorted tile indices.

DONE WHEN: history_sweep reports overseas holdings per major at the epoch and the distribution is wide; a polity with no harbour work never founds across water (asserted); world_determinism on the 0 CE arc unchanged.

--- WHAT THE SUBSYSTEM MAP FOUND, 2026-09-03 (amends the premise above) ---

THE PREMISE ABOVE IS WRONG IN ONE IMPORTANT WAY. "The sim knows nothing about water" is false. Region adjacency is water-blind at neighbour_radius 9, so short overseas campaigns are ALREADY legal and free (BL-755), and the Settle verb founds on ocean without a terrain test (BL-756). This item therefore PRICES AND GATES an existing capability; both prerequisites must be settled first, and the "before" figure for any sea-leg measurement is not zero.

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE, and cheaper than expected: the sim ALREADY HOLDS THE COASTLINE. sim_terrain_view::substrate (history_sim.hpp:81) is the raster substrate array in row*gw+col order, populated verbatim from tile.substrate by build_sim_terrain, and it carries ocean / lake / coast. A deterministic coastal walk is expressible on the EXISTING view with no signature change, no world& and no ECS access - which preserves the sim's deliberate world-free design (history_sim.hpp:70-75). The substrate is fixed at generation and nothing rewrites it (components.hpp:545-546), so a per-body walk may be precomputed once.

THE HARD CONSTRAINTS. (1) INTEGER FIXED-POINT ONLY in the decision path (history_sim.hpp:24-28); every campaign-era pathfinding structure (tile_traversal_cost, flood_field_for, body_reach_field, logistics_path) is float-valued and CANNOT be reused. (2) Price the leg inside campaign_supply (history_sim.cpp:572), never beside it - pricing supply in two places is the BL-318 defect the comment at 545-566 records. (3) is_sea (components.hpp:378), never is_water: the campaign era's crosses_ocean reads is_water and so flips on a single lake tile, which is what sea_leg_census exists to measure. (4) Adding a candidate to the scorer changes the argmax even when it never wins, so the ancient arc must be gated to execute identically or world_determinism's 0 CE digests move.

STILL OPEN, and needing Ben before this is buildable: which walk (coast tiles only vs all is_sea) and how the four harbour rows map onto ranges, given nothing in the code labels a sea "enclosed"; where the walk is anchored, since a region has no harbour tile and adding one is a save-format change; how "holds a harbour work" is tested, since work_row has no harbour flag; whether the naval roster rows (Coastal Galley, Broadside Ship, Ironclad - all base power 0 and skipped by sum_stack) gain real power here or stay inert; and whether an overseas daughter region re-surveys port_q instead of inheriting 0.7x.

--- LARGELY DISSOLVED BY THE WATER-DOMAIN RULING (Ben, 2026-09-06) ---

This item was to build a sea-leg candidate channel: a coastal walk, harbour rows mapped to ranges, a supply cost priced through campaign_supply. Under the water-domain model most of that falls out rather than being built. A "sea leg" is just a path whose domains require a naval traversal capability (BL-778), and the units that may take it are the naval rows made real by BL-779.

What survives of this item: the harbour works still want a reason to exist beyond reach_mod, and the question of whether a coastal province can hold a port is still open. The five design calls recorded above are mostly answered by the ruling - which walk, how the harbour rows map to ranges, and how "holds a harbour work" is tested all collapse into "which domains does this unit declare".

Re-scope or close this item before building it; it should not be built as filed.
--- REQUIRES REPOINTED 2026-09-06: THE WATER MODEL IS NOW THIS ITEM FOUNDATION ---

BL-755 and BL-756 are closed superseded by BL-778 and BL-777, so this item no longer waits on
them. It waits on the water model itself, which gives it three things it previously had to invent:
  * a REAL sea test. region gains a domain (land / coastal_water / open_ocean) from BL-777, so the
    sea-access gate stops keying on port_q - which is a decayed wetness fraction that counts LAKES
    and is inherited at 0.7x without re-survey. That was BL-756 second finding and it is the one
    thing from that row that had to survive it.
  * a LEGALITY model instead of a pricing model. BL-778 makes crossing a domain question, so the
    sea leg is gated rather than penalised.
  * NAVAL ROWS THAT ARE WORTH SOMETHING. BL-779 answers call (4) of NR-785 outright.

NR-785 THEREFORE SHRINKS FROM FIVE CALLS TO THREE. Answered by the water model: (4) do the naval
rows gain real power - YES, BL-779. Partly answered: (2) where the walk is anchored, since
BL-777 already bumps the save format for region, so a harbour anchor field costs no extra
migration. STILL OPEN AND STILL BEN: (1) which walk - coast tiles only or all is_sea - and how the
four harbour rows map onto ranges; (3) how "holds a harbour work" is tested, since work_row has no
harbour flag; (5) whether an overseas daughter re-surveys port_q or inherits it.
--- AUTHORITY REASSIGNED 2026-09-06 (Ben, on the military-history split form) ---

This item's home is docs/generation/MILITARY_HISTORY.md § Sea legs and colonisation, which did
not exist when the item was filed. The five open calls are recorded there as well as here, and the
corrected premise NR-785 raised is now stated in an authority doc rather than living only in a
review entry: the sim does not LACK overseas reach, it has too much - water-blind Chebyshev
adjacency at radius 9, 43% of adjacency edges crossing sea, and regions founded on ocean with 0
defence. The 'before' figure is not zero.

WHAT UNBLOCKS IT is the legality test from BL-778, not a supply penalty. The five calls remain
open and none should be guessed.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: Pass 2's colonial ties seed the order book's preferred-seller relationships, so a colony's chains close through its metropole first
items.design:
THE LEVER. The order book already honours a buyer's preferred_seller, served first and tolerated up to 1.10x the cheapest compatible ask (MARKETS.md step 10). Nothing sets it at generation. Pass 2 (BL-749, sea-leg campaign) produces ownership history - which metropole held which colony, and for how long - and that is exactly the fact a trade tie should be derived from.

THE DESIGN. At handoff, for each region that was an overseas holding at the epoch or within N years of it, firms placed there carry a preferred_seller toward the metropole nation's firms for the goods the colony cannot close itself (the chain-completeness read says which). A tie, not a rule: the 1.10x tolerance is the whole strength of it, and a cheaper local seller beyond that tolerance wins. This is the third of the three forces in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Three passes - tariffs, distance, ties - and the one that makes "global trade" a set of ROUTES with a history rather than a uniform pull toward the cheapest ask.

DONE WHEN: haulage_measure on a 1960 world shows convoy traffic on colony<->metropole legs above the baseline; removing the ties (params) removes it; determinism unchanged.
--- REQUIRES REPOINTED (2026-09-06, consequence of BL-751 being cancelled) ---

This item required BL-751 (economic settle pass) for the field the ties are applied to. BL-751 is
cancelled superseded, so the require moves to BL-770 (Era 0 candidate search), which is what now
produces the corporate landscape a tie can be drawn across. Nothing about the tie design changes -
the preferred_seller seam and the 1.10x tolerance are untouched.

STILL GATED ON BL-749 (sea-leg campaign), and that is the binding one: a colonial tie needs an
ownership history to derive from, and BL-749 is itself held on the five design calls recorded at
NR-785. So this item is not reachable in the current wave regardless of the BL-770 repoint.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: One seed-sweep instrument for the three passes - chain-completeness spread, the lapse four, the haulage baseline, the sweep distributions - read as distributions, never as per-world targets
items.design:
"GAMIFYING GENERATION" MEANS A SCOREBOARD, NOT A TARGET. Ben, 2026-08-31: no start is clamped up to viability or down to fairness; generation owes the SPREAD. The three passes are tuned by moving a force (a weight in history_sim_params, a tariff threshold, the settle's spawn cadence) and reading how the DISTRIBUTION across a seed spread moves. The instruments exist and are read one at a time; this item puts them on one sheet.

THE WORK. A sweep target (run_sweep.cmake already fans harnesses over seeds) that, per seed, records: chain-completeness spread (demand_census R5 - min, median, max, tails); the lapse four at handoff (mean operating net, operating-positive corps, valued production, debtors); the haulage baseline (convoy count and cargo vs the 1055/802 reference - goldens cannot see trade); and history_sweep's pass-1/pass-2 outputs (nation count, furnace years, overseas holdings, tariffed nations). One table, seeds as rows, printed and diffable. No assertion beyond "the spread is not zero" - the instrument reports, the sprint argues.

DONE WHEN: the sheet exists, runs over the standard seed spread in one command, and sprint 32's retro cites it.

items.author: Ben (design session 2026-09-03, "gamify generation"); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: The generating-screen budget for three passes - measure first, then re-file only the affordability rungs the measurement demands
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-03: "I am interested to see if this can be done cheaply. This is in fact a difficult abstraction problem." The budget is the generating screen's wait (~25-38 s generation + ~6 s warm start today, per app.cpp). Pass 1 is already the most expensive pass; pass 2 doubles it and pass 3 lengthens the settle by an order of magnitude at 4 ticks a year. Cost tracks the province table, not the fighting (COLLAPSE.md § The 4000-year problem).

THE WORK. (1) Instrument the wait per pass on the loading screen's progress sink and in history_sweep, so every sprint-32 item records its cost on this item as it lands. (2) The affordability rungs in COLLAPSE.md § The 4000-year problem - kill the O(provinces) scans, quiet-province fast path, banded year grain, record on change - were purged with the ancient pivot and are NOT re-filed here in advance. Re-file the one the measurement points at, when it does, in that order. (3) The abstraction question Ben names is the handoff between two engines, not either engine: keep the handoff a struct of plain outputs (regions, works, strain, ties, posture) so pass 3 never reads pass 2's internals.

DONE WHEN: a 1960 world with all three passes generates inside a budget Ben has stated on this item; if it cannot, the item records which rung buys it back and that rung is filed.

--- MEASURED 2026-09-03, the instrumentation half landed with BL-747 ---

  0 CE, 400 y      total 8200 ms = pre-settlement 443 + settlement 4 + ERA-1 323 + post-era 7428
  0 CE, no era     total 6661 ms = pre-settlement 455 + settlement 3 + ERA-1   0 + post-era 6202
  1960, two-span   total 7996 ms = pre-settlement 465 + settlement 2 + ERA-1 197 + post-era 7331

THE ANSWER TO BEN'S QUESTION IS YES, AND BY A WIDER MARGIN THAN EXPECTED. The second span is not merely affordable, it is FREE: 800 simulated years at epoch 1960 cost 197 ms against 323 ms for 400 years at 0 CE, and the whole 1960 world builds FASTER than the 0 CE one. The reason is the one COLLAPSE.md § The 4000-year problem already states - cost tracks the province/region table, not the fighting or the years - and at 1960 the settlement pass has already founded most regions, so the sim founds 506 where the ancient arc founds 833.

THE SECOND FINDING IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES BUDGETING. The era pass costs about FOUR TIMES its own wall clock. Era on versus off at 0 CE is a ~1.5 s difference, of which only 323 ms is the sim itself; the remaining ~1.2 s is every pass after it working over the 833 regions the era founded. A budget taken off the era's own timer is wrong by 4x, and the affordability rungs in COLLAPSE.md are aimed at the 323 ms rather than the 1.2 s.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE REMAINING RUNGS. None of them is needed yet. The 4000-year ladder (BL-494) is the case that would test them, and the right next measurement is a 4000-year ancient span at epoch 1960 rather than any optimisation. Do not re-file a rung until a measurement points at it.

STILL OPEN on this item: the budget Ben will actually state, and the settle pass's own cost (BL-751), which is gated on sprint 33.

--- TWO GAPS FOUND IN THE PLAY BUILD, 2026-09-03 ---

(1) THE GAME NEVER REPORTS ITS OWN GENERATION BUDGET. The "[gen budget]" line added with this item is inside the "if (fixture)" branch in hard_coded_world.cpp, and the app passes fixture = nullptr. So every number this item quotes is a HARNESS number, and the loading screen - which work item (1) explicitly named as the place to instrument - still says nothing about where its wait goes. Remaining work on this item, not a completed half.

(2) THE BUDGET IS NOT WHERE THIS ITEM WAS LOOKING. Measured in the release play build, the warm start is 72-73 s on BOTH arcs against generation's ~8 s. The pass this item exists to price (197-323 ms) is under half a percent of the startup wait. That does not make the era measurement wrong, but it does mean "can generation afford more complexity" is the wrong question to ask of the startup budget: generation is not what the player is waiting for. BL-761 owns the warm start.
--- REQUIRES REPOINTED 2026-09-06 (consequence of BL-751 being cancelled) ---

This item required BL-751 (economic settle pass) because the settle was the pass whose wall
clock it had to budget. BL-751 is cancelled superseded, so the require moves to BL-770 (Era 0
candidate search), which is the pass that now carries that burden.

AND ITS PREMISE IS PARTLY OVERTAKEN. The item says "the app still never prints its own
generation budget" - but world_determinism already emits a [gen budget] line per generated
world (total ms, split pre-settlement / settlement / era-1 / post-era), observed 2026-09-06
at ~6.5 s total with post-era dominating at 5.9 s. So the MEASUREMENT exists in the harness
tier; what is still missing is the APP printing it on its own generating screen. Re-scope to
that half before building.
--- DELIVERED 2026-09-06 (console half proved; on-screen half UNVERIFIED) ---

generation_progress gains five atomic budget fields plus a release-stored budget_ready. That
struct is ALREADY the app-to-generation seam, already atomic, and already a write-only tap with NO
save-format presence - which is why the clock goes there rather than on generation_report (which
is serialised) or era_minus_one_fixture (a heavy capture the app never asks for). NO SERIALISATION
SEAM IS OWED, and that is a design consequence rather than an omission.

The stderr [gen budget] line stays gated on `fixture`, so harness-tier output is unchanged.
app::begin_new_game CLEARS the budget - without that a second campaign would show the previous
world split, which is the kind of stale-read nobody notices until it misleads someone.

MEASURED FROM THE WORKTREE: [gen budget] total 53005 ms (pre-settlement 2016, settlement 48,
era-1 7365, post-era 43575).

R1 IS NOT MARKED COMPLETE. The console half is proved; the ON-SCREEN half is not. The agent could
not take a live look - computer-use access was denied and the granted path resolved to a DIFFERENT
worktree exe, which is the known granted-path trap. A clean compile is not evidence that a surface
renders, and the standing rule is that a UI requirement needs a live click. OWED: open the built
app and look at the generating screen.

items.author: Cold review of the BL-747 diff, 2026-09-03
items.title: The 1960 arc now gains era-seeded demography as a side effect of BL-747, and era_world_harness R2 is red because of it - a design-red for Ben, not a harness to re-bless
items.design:
FOUND by the cold review of BL-747, 2026-09-03. The main session's own verification MISSED it: world_determinism was green and era_world_harness was never run.

THE CHAIN. era_minus_one_enabled now returns true at epoch 1960, so run_history_sim runs there. history_sim.cpp:332 unconditionally seeds every zero-population region (population = region_carrying_capacity(farm_q) / 8). settlement.cpp:544 deliberately leaves 1960-epoch regions at population 0 - the antiquity branch is the only seeding path. So 1960 regions go from 0 to roughly carrying capacity, and era_world_harness R2 ("the 1960 world stays demography-unseeded, graduation not its path") fails: 12 passed, 1 failed.

IT IS WIDER THAN ONE HARNESS ROW. That population feeds generate_population_centres (hard_coded_world.cpp:679), derive_national_character, and nation and corporation generation. The 1960 world's demography, politics and corporate seeding all move. HISTORY.md, the BL-747 requirement rows and the diff comments are all silent on it.

WHY IT IS BEN'S CALL AND NOT A FIX. Two defensible readings. (a) It is CORRECT and intended: the sim ran, it founded 506 regions, and regions with people are what a run produces - the harness asserts a property BL-747 deliberately overturns, and should be re-aimed with the change recorded in HISTORY.md. (b) It is a SIDE EFFECT nobody asked for: BL-747's subject is the span structure, and silently re-basing 1960 demography is scope the item never claimed. Under (b) the seeding should be gated so it only fires where settlement left the regions unseeded by design.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE HARNESS TO PASS. It is red for a real reason and stays red until Ben rules. Whichever way it goes, the 0 CE arc is unaffected - world_determinism's three digests are unmoved either way.

CONFIRMED IN THE MAIN SESSION 2026-09-03, not taken on the reviewer word. Built era_world_harness on the committed tree (build_lua_harness.bat, Release path) and ran it:

  PASS  R2 every 0 CE region holds population within (0, capacity]
  PASS  R2 manpower sits within its population ceiling
  FAIL  R2 the 1960 world stays demography-unseeded (graduation not its path)
  12 passed, 1 failed

So the 0 CE half of R2 is untouched and only the 1960 clause moved, which is exactly what the chain predicts and narrows the question to the one Ben has to answer. The harness is LEFT RED.

items.author: Claude (measured in the play build, 2026-09-03)
items.title: The warm start is 72 seconds on BOTH arcs - 12x its budget, and it dwarfs everything generation does
items.design:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 in the RELEASE play build (build_rel), running the app twice with --autostart:

  epoch 1960 (two-span)   warm_start_80_ticks  73167 ms   convoys 14763.9 | run_economy_step 57023.9
  epoch 0    (ancient)    warm_start_80_ticks  72088 ms   convoys 28321.1 | run_economy_step 42361.6

THE HEADLINE: THE TWO ARCS COST THE SAME, so this is NOT caused by BL-747. The 0 CE arc is byte-identical across that change (digests unmoved), and it pays 72.1 s where the new two-span 1960 arc pays 73.2 s. The warm start was already this expensive; running the sim at 1960 added roughly a second. Filed separately from BL-754 for exactly that reason - it is the startup cost the player actually waits through, and it belongs to the economy tick, not to generation.

THE SCALE OF THE MISMATCH. app.cpp's own comment budgets "the ~25-38 s generation plus ~6 s warm start that follow it". The warm start is running at 12x that. And it dwarfs the thing this sprint has been optimising: the Era -1 sim is 197-323 ms, generation end to end is ~8 s in the Release harness path, and the warm start is 72 s. Any conversation about whether generation can afford more complexity is answered by this number - generation is not where the startup budget goes.

WHERE IT GOES, and the two arcs split differently, which is the useful part:
  * run_economy_step dominates both, but MORE on the industrial band (57.0 s vs 42.4 s) - more recipes, more buildings, deeper chains.
  * convoys are the reverse (14.8 s industrial vs 28.3 s ancient), which is worth understanding on its own: the ancient arc spends nearly twice as long moving goods. Candidate cause is the ancient chain being shallower, so more raw tonnage moves further, but that is a hypothesis and not a measurement.
  * Everything else is noise: clear_markets ~0.11 s, apply_budget ~0.77 s, history_recorders ~0.39 s.

THE WORK, in order. (1) Profile run_economy_step across the 80 warm ticks and find what is O(n^2) or rebuilding per tick - 42-57 s over 80 ticks is 530-710 ms PER TICK, which is also what the player pays per tick at speed once playing, so this is a play-speed problem wearing a loading-screen costume. (2) Same for the convoy pass. (3) Only then consider reducing pre_game_ticks, which would be treating the symptom - the settle wants MORE ticks, not fewer (BL-751 makes the warm start a real generation pass).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE WAIT: BL-751 (economic settle pass) proposes lengthening this pass by an order of magnitude so firms spawn and exit until the field is steady. At 0.9 s a tick that is not affordable, and BL-751's gate should read this item as well as sprint 33's growth half.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 2 - tiles ride plates, and a tile can be asked where it was and what its climate was at age T
items.design:
THE AIM: the second and deepest of the three gaps behind Ben's "realistically mapping the landform from ancient life to modern resources" (point 2). BL-763 gives drift a clock; this gives it a frame of reference.

THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM, and it does not go away by adding a loop. plate_id (continents.cpp:112) answers "which plate SEED is nearest this fixed grid cell". Tiles do not ride plates. Even with drifting seeds you get a Voronoi partition that reshuffles under stationary ground, not ground that moves - so "this tile was at the equator in the Carboniferous" is not expressible.

AND PALEO-LATITUDE IS THE SAME PROBLEM IN ITS SHARPEST FORM. Latitude is band_for_row(row) - THE GRID ROW ITSELF (tile_generation.cpp:314). A tile's climate band is fixed for all time by where it sits in the raster. There is no representation in which a tile HAD a different latitude, which is precisely what a coal-forming swamp at a tropical palaeolatitude requires.

THE THIRD GAP, PALEO-CLIMATE: nothing computes moisture, temperature or cover at a past epoch. theta_at (planetology.cpp:952) is the only past-state reconstructor and it returns a body-GLOBAL thermal scalar, not a per-tile climate. There is no climate_at(tile, age).

SCOPE HONESTLY. This is a representation change to the oldest layer in the generator, and every pass downstream reads its output. It is the single largest item in the reorder and should be split again at promotion rather than taken whole. A cheaper intermediate exists and was NOT chosen (a present-landform proxy, form option (b)) - Ben took the real one, so it is filed at its real size.

DONE WHEN: a tile can be asked for its position and climate band at a given age, deterministically; the present-day answer is identical to today's, so nothing downstream moves until BL-765 reads the past.
--- SLICE 1 DELIVERED 2026-09-06: THE QUERY, NOT THE FRAME ---

paleo_tile_at(cs, gw, gh, col, row, epochs_back, temp, moisture) returns past column/row,
pole-folded latitude, lat_band, and moisture sampled AT THE PAST POSITION. band_for_row was
promoted out of its anonymous namespace and split into band_for_distance, so the paleo path reads
the SAME table Pass 3 does rather than a copy - the two-callers-one-implementation discipline that
BL-775 was about.

FOUR THINGS DELIBERATELY LEFT, each stated in CONTINENTS.md § The boundary of the frame:
  1. THE GENERATOR DOES NOT RUN IN THE MOVING FRAME. Pass 3 still bands by present row and must -
     banding by a past row changes every world. The frame is a QUERY over the finished world.
  2. No past height, cover or ocean. Only position and climate wind back.
  3. No longitude flip across a pole. Latitude folds, the column does not; ~24 rows of 121 over the
     full 100 My are affected, and the harness reports the count (520 sampled pairs off-grid) with
     on_grid=false rather than handing back a silently clamped sample.
  4. No body-global palaeo-thermal term. theta_at is a lambda inside run_planetology and exporting
     it needs new PERSISTENT fields on planetology_state - the serialisation seam - for a term that
     moves under 1% over 100 My. planetology.cpp was not touched at all.

NO DIGEST MOVED. All four at their recorded values; deposit total 5303910.684 unchanged.
A MODELLING CALL WAS TAKEN AND IS FLAGGED: a stagnant lid is IMMOBILE in the paleo frame, on the
authority of CONTINENTS.md and continent_snapshot_at own early return. It made a red harness row
green, which is the shape of weakening a test even when it is not one - so it is NR-787 for Ben.
--- STILL OPEN 2026-09-06, DELIBERATELY ---

Slice 1 (the paleo QUERY) landed and BL-765 now consumes it. What remains is the FRAME: the
generator still bands by present row and must, because banding by a past row changes every world.
Also unbuilt: past height/cover/ocean, the longitude flip across a pole, and the body-global
palaeo-thermal term. All four boundaries are stated in CONTINENTS.md § The boundary of the frame.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: Phase 8 - retire the warm start and the background-firm pass; phase 6 carries their burden
items.design:
THE AIM (Ben, point 8): "I think we should retire this phase and push the burden onto phase 6."

IT IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST BUDGET WIN AVAILABLE, AND IT IS MEASURED. The warm start is 72-73 SECONDS in the release play build, on BOTH arcs, against the ~6 s app.cpp budgets for it (BL-761). It is most of the ~2 minutes generation takes today, which matches Ben's own estimate that "most of that is Phase 7". Retiring it frees the entire budget that phase 6's candidate search needs.

IT IS ALSO THE RIGHT DESIGN, not just the cheap one. The warm start is 80 undirected ticks that settle whatever generation happened to place. Phase 6 is 400 directed years that CHOOSE the corporate landscape. Keeping both would be paying twice for the weaker answer.

WHAT GOES: app::start_new_game's pre_game_ticks loop and its sliced-progress UI, and Pass 6 background-firm generation as a separate one-shot (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 6) - the firms phase 6 selects ARE the background economy.

THIS SUPERSEDES BL-751 (economic settle pass) AS DESIGNED. That item was the warm start PROMOTED - the same pass, longer, with spawn and cull. Ben's ordering replaces it with a directed search. BL-751 should be rewritten around phase 6 or closed as superseded; it must not be built as filed.

WHAT MUST NOT BE LOST: the warm start exists so play opens on a settled position rather than a cold one, and the clock is rebased so play always begins at the epoch (BL-369). Phase 6 has to hand over a world in that same settled state, and ERAS.md's "the warm start has no calendar meaning" paragraph needs rewriting rather than deleting.

DONE WHEN: no pre_game_ticks loop remains; a world handed to play is settled by phase 6; startup time drops by ~72 s; ERAS.md and MARKETS.md § Background corporations describe the new source of the background economy.
--- BLOCKED 2026-09-06, ON EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS PREDICTED TO BE BLOCKED ON. NO CODE MOVED ---

PHASE 6 HAS NO SEARCH. BL-770 delivered its scorer, and slice 2 taught that scorer to see a roster
- but there is still no candidate generation, no argmax, and no selection wired into generation.
Confirmed independently by the implementer: src/world/landscape_score.cpp has NO CALLER outside
tools/verify/landscape_score_harness.cpp.

So retiring the warm start today would open play on an UNSETTLED position, which is worse than the
72-73 seconds it would save. app::pre_game_ticks and Pass 6 one-shot both STAY. The brief
pre-authorised this outcome and the agent took it rather than trading correctness for a wall clock.

R5 (the startup drop) therefore reads ZERO SECONDS, and is recorded as failed rather than quietly
dropped: the item has not delivered its headline.

WHAT DID LAND IS R4, and it was worth landing alone. ERAS.md and MARKETS.md were both asserting
something GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § The eight phases had already overturned - the silent-doc case.
ERAS.md warm-start paragraph is REWRITTEN into two: the calendar rebase (the load-bearing,
pass-independent half - play opens at epoch_year and the opening position owes the calendar
nothing), and then what settles it is a SEARCH, not a settle. MARKETS.md § Background corporations
now sources the background economy from the landscape phase 6 selects, and EXPLAINS the superseded
~90%-of-demand stopping rule rather than dropping it: a target fraction pushes every market toward
the same coverage, which is the evenness § Asymmetry is the deliverable exists to prevent.

UNBLOCKS ON: BL-770 slice 3, the search itself.

items.author: Ben (the 8-point generation reorder, 2026-09-03, with the five calls taken on the elicitation form); Claude (itemisation, against the feasibility pass)
items.title: The reorder measured against Ben 3-6 minute generation budget, per phase, with the parallel plan asserted
items.design:
THE TARGET (Ben, 2026-09-03): "I'm aiming to have generation take anywhere from 3-6 minutes. The current generation takes about 2 minutes, and most of that is Phase 7."

THE ARITHMETIC AS IT STANDS, measured 2026-09-03. Today: ~2 min, of which the warm start is 72-73 s (BL-761) - Ben's estimate confirmed. Retiring it (BL-772) returns ~72 s. Phase 6 at six candidates is 53-71 s EACH serially, which would be 5.3-7.1 min and break the budget; in parallel on 16 logical cores it is ~1 min of wall clock. So the reorder's headline cost is roughly: generation once + ~1 min of parallel search, leaving real headroom for the extra complexity phases 1-5 add.

WHAT THIS ITEM OWNS: keeping that arithmetic true as each phase lands. Every item in the reorder records its measured cost here as it completes, and the total is checked against 3-6 minutes rather than assumed. BL-754 already instruments per-pass timing, and its unfinished half - the app never prints the budget because the [gen budget] line only fires when a harness passes a fixture - must land here, because a budget nobody can see in the game is not a budget.

THE RISK TO WATCH, stated up front: the era pass costs ~4x its own wall clock, because everything downstream works over the regions it founded. Phases 1-5 all ADD founded detail. So the cheap-looking additions are the ones to measure, not the expensive-looking ones.

DONE WHEN: a full reordered generation is timed per phase in the play build, the total sits in 3-6 minutes, and the app itself reports it.

items.author: Claude (relied on the flag all session before noticing)
items.title: backlog_query silently ignores an unknown flag, so --sprint returns everything and reads as a filtered result
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-06, after relying on it repeatedly. `backlog_query.js --sprint 32b` returns BL-714 (sprint null) and BL-733 (sprint "29") among its rows. `--sprint` is not in the supported filter set - the help lists --status, --priority, --version, --category, --touches, --grep, --fields, --count, --all - so it is parsed as nothing, ignored, and the tool prints EVERY open item. A caller reading the output sees a plausible, shorter-looking list and takes it for a filtered one.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. This is the same class as the four instruments 32a turned up: an output that looks like an answer to the question asked, and is an answer to a different one. It is worse than an error, because an unknown flag that errors costs five seconds and an unknown flag that is ignored costs a wrong conclusion. In this session it was caught only because two items whose sprint I happened to know appeared in a list they could not belong to.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE OF DISCIPLINE, not a feature: reject an unrecognised argument and name it, rather than ignoring it. Apply to the sibling query tools at the same time - requirements_query.js and actions_query.js take the same shape and are likely to have the same hole.

WORTH CONSIDERING WHILE THERE: --sprint is a filter people evidently expect to exist (this session assumed it three times), and every item carries a sprint field. Adding it is cheap; but the rejection is the actual bug and should land even if the filter does not.

DONE WHEN: an unknown flag exits non-zero naming the flag; the three query tools share that behaviour.

items.author: Ben (spotted live, 2026-09-06); Claude (itemisation)
items.title: One nation comes out with a COMPLETE road lattice - every internal edge stamped, which is not what a trunk route looks like
items.design:
SPOTTED BY BEN IN THE LIVE APP (2026-09-06), looking at the world BL-768 had just built: one nation
carries a COMPLETE LATTICE of roads - effectively every internal edge stamped - while its
neighbours carry the sparse trunk shape the item intended.

I SAW THE SAME THING AND TALKED MYSELF OUT OF IT, which is worth recording because it is the
failure mode the session kept hitting. Zooming the canvas I noted the density looked near-total and
did not match BL-768 own measured +320 roaded tiles, then looked at a different region, found it
sparser, and moved on. The aggregate was right and the per-nation distribution was wrong, and an
aggregate cannot see that.

THE LIKELY MECHANISM, to be confirmed rather than assumed. BL-768 records a corridor at TWO sites:
the campaign path records (staging holding, objective), and the SETTLE path records (parent,
daughter) for every founding. The run is settle-dominated by design (NR-205, ruled 2026-08-12) -
the era report shows 833 foundings against 270 battles on seed A. So a polity that expanded by
settling outward has a recorded corridor from every parent to every daughter, which over a
contiguous holding IS a spanning lattice. The measured corridor histogram is consistent: 3185
corridors of which 3119 walked exactly once - a huge population of single-use edges, which is what
a founding tree looks like rather than a trade network.

WHY THE THRESHOLD DID NOT CATCH IT: kAncientRoadUses = 4 gates the ROAD tier, but a single-use
corridor still stamps a TRACK. So the lattice is real road_level, just at the bottom rung.

THE DESIGN QUESTION UNDERNEATH, and it is not a tuning one: is a founding line a TRADE corridor at
all? A parent settling a daughter walked that ground once. A supply line walked forty times is a
road. LOGISTICS.md wants roads that supply provinces - traffic, not ancestry. The likely fix is to
weight or exclude the settle corridors rather than to raise the threshold, but that is a call.

MEASURE FIRST, and the instrument is owed as much as the fix: road_reach_census reports totals and
C6 reports an era ON/OFF delta, but NOTHING reports the PER-NATION distribution of roaded tiles or
road density against holding size. A per-nation row would have caught this before it reached the
canvas, and is the thing that makes the fix checkable.

DONE WHEN: no nation carries a road lattice materially denser than its neighbours for a reason
unrelated to its traffic; the per-nation density spread is reported; and the settle-vs-campaign
corridor question is answered explicitly rather than by a constant.

items.author: Claude (found by lane B against MILITARY.md § Domains and traversal, 2026-09-07)
items.title: The placement seam admits a port on owned coastal water - the one building the design allows there
items.design:
THE DESIGN IS WRITTEN AND THE CODE REFUSES IT. docs/military/MILITARY.md § Domains and traversal
(Ben, 2026-09-06): 'A coastal province holds a port, and nothing else.' placement_rules::can_place
opens with a blanket `if (is_water_tile(...)) return ocean` - every building, port included.

SO BL-785's CONSTRUCT PREDICATE IS DEAD ON ARRIVAL. The UI half is built and correct: it offers
Construct only for a port, only on coastal water, only where tile_to_nation holds the tile. That
predicate evaluates FALSE on every tile in every world, because the seam beneath it refuses water
before the type is ever considered.

THE WORK. can_place admits building_type::port on a tile whose substrate is coastal water or lake
AND whose tile carries a nation. Open ocean stays refused - structurally unowned, so the ownership
clause already excludes it, but assert that rather than relying on it.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE CHANGE, and why lane B correctly did not take it: can_place is the
SHARED placement seam. The rival scorer (corp_ai.cpp) reads it to build its candidate list, so
admitting a water port immediately puts water ports in every background corporation's build
candidates and MOVES SIMULATED OUTCOMES. That is a world-moving change and it owes the digest
discipline in DELIVERY.md § The digest re-bless is one act per WAVE.

ORDERING: this should land AFTER BL-780's re-bless, not before. The wave already carries four
causes; a fifth that changes what every rival builds is exactly what that item exists to prevent.

OPEN AND NOT TO BE GUESSED: whether a water port differs from a land port in what it DOES is
docs/economy/LOGISTICS.md's question. This item only makes it placeable.

DONE WHEN: a port places on owned coastal water and nowhere else on water; open ocean refuses;
world_audit asserts both; and the BL-785 Construct button goes live, confirmed by a click.
